note: Dated events that explain the regimes in the sample, one document each, in this study's words. An event no readable document supports is not a row; left_out lists them with the reason.

events.what: The first export cargo of the shale era leaves Sabine Pass, the Asia Vision, for Brazil.
events.publisher: US Department of Energy, LNG monthly reports, transaction file

events.what: US cargoes cancelled as the pandemic cut demand: about 46 in June and 50 in July by EIA's estimate, 45 for August and about 30 for September by the trade press reports EIA cites.
events.publisher: U.S. Energy Information Administration, Today in Energy, 11 August 2020

events.what: Delays at Panama of 12 days reported for vessels without a booked slot.
The last LNG cargo crosses the Red Sea: after the Houthi attacks on shipping, none crossed from 12 January 2024 to the end of February.
events.publisher: Oxford Institute for Energy Studies, NG 188, February 2024

events.what: A record 27 US cargoes to Asia sail round the Cape of Good Hope in the month.
events.publisher: Platts, republished by Hellenic Shipping News, 22 April 2024

events.what: The first LNG carrier in five months passes Bab el Mandeb.
China's tariff on US LNG takes effect, 15 percent by this account; a later report gives 25 percent, and the Chinese notice itself was not read.
events.publisher: Columbia University, Center on Global Energy Policy, 18 April 2025

events.what: The US and China are reported to be discussing a cut to China's tariff on US LNG.
events.publisher: gCaptain, 19 September 2026, reporting Reuters of 18 September

left_out.what: JKM's record low of 28 April 2020, Cape voyages above one a day in November 2020 and 58 LNG transits of Panama in January 2021
left_out.reason: S&P Global's figures; this study does not request S&P Global's pages and found no republication of these

left_out.what: Russia's invasion of Ukraine on 24 February 2022
left_out.reason: no document on it was read for this study; the year shows in the spread, TTF above JKM for long stretches

left_out.what: The first attacks on shipping in the Red Sea, November 2023
left_out.reason: no dated document on them was read; the closure of the route is marked from January 2024

left_out.what: The Suez Canal Authority's rebates for US Gulf LNG carriers and Panama's slot auctions
left_out.reason: rules of the canals, not events: they are in the tolls and on the Routes view's timeline

left_out.what: No US cargo reaching China from 6 February 2025
left_out.reason: a statement of April 2025 about arrivals, which EIA's table contradicts for September 2025

left_out.what: The closure of the Strait of Hormuz on 28 February 2026, and Spark's Atlantic rate jumping 163 percent on 3 March 2026
left_out.reason: EIA's article on Hormuz was read but not for that date; the jump is Lloyd's List's figure, which this study does not request; LNG Prime's 161,750 $/day for 3 March is drawn as a charter rate

left_out.what: The JKM to TTF spread flipping from a European to an Asian premium in March 2026
left_out.reason: IEA's averages were not read; the spread itself is drawn

left_out.what: The US and Iran memorandum of 14 June 2026 and the hostilities of July 2026
left_out.reason: no document on them was read

left_out.what: US LNG to China in June 2026, one cargo and part of another
left_out.reason: the wording waits on the owner, and whether the cargo was imported or re-exported is not established

left_out.what: JKM and TTF reported on 18 September 2026 with the US arbitrage to Asia uneconomic
left_out.reason: Global LNG Hub's note was not read

left_out.what: Spark's first negative Atlantic rate, 8 February 2022, and its record of 374,000 $/day in October 2022
left_out.reason: charter rates, drawn as such on the breakeven hire panel

left_out.what: The EU ETS covering shipping and Spark's change of ship, January 2024
left_out.reason: breaks in the data, drawn as numbered rules
